01 / Website UX · D2C2024 — Present

KILRR Website

Designing the brand’s direct-to-consumer website around a simple task: help people understand the product, choose a flavour and move confidently towards purchase.

Information architectureProduct discoveryPage designAnalytics
Explore the case study
The experience to solve

KILRR sells ready-to-use marinades and gravy masalas. The website needs to explain an unfamiliar product format quickly, make a growing flavour range easy to browse, and reduce friction between discovery and checkout.

My role

Creative Lead and UI/UX Designer. I led the website experience and visual direction, connecting brand expression with the practical structure of a D2C storefront.

What I worked on
  • Structured the browsing experience around product categories, flavour discovery and bundles.
  • Designed the product storytelling hierarchy so the use case, flavour proposition and purchase information are easier to scan.
  • Worked across product listing and product detail experiences, promotional modules and purchase touchpoints.
  • Connected brand-led storytelling with functional information such as preparation steps, shipping and product FAQs.
Analytics-informed evaluation

I used website analytics as a behavioural lens to assess how visitors move from landing and product discovery towards purchase. The key checkpoints for this experience are:

DiscoverEntry pages · category engagement
EvaluateProduct views · product interactions
ConvertAdd-to-cart · checkout progression

Performance figures are intentionally not published here. Add validated analytics screenshots or before/after values before making conversion-lift claims.

What this project demonstrates

Balancing a distinctive brand voice with clear navigation, product comprehension and a purchase journey that has to work as well as it looks.

02 / Interaction design · AndroidPrototype

Motorcycle Companion App

A phone-first companion experience exploring how essential media controls can stay usable when a rider’s attention belongs on the road.

Interaction designControl mappingAndroid StudioVoice-ready exploration
Explore the case study
The interaction problem

Touch interfaces are not always practical while riding. The concept explores a more direct relationship between the motorcycle’s existing handlebar joystick and the phone experience, especially for media controls.

My role

Independent product concept and prototype. I designed and built the Android experience, then explored how the app could respond to the bike’s existing media-control inputs.

Interaction principles
  • Keep frequent media actions simple and predictable.
  • Map supported handlebar inputs to familiar playback controls.
  • Make connection state and control feedback easy to understand.
  • Explore voice as a future hands-free layer, not as a shipped feature.
Prototype status

The Android app is a working personal prototype. The current exploration covers touch interaction and media control through the motorcycle’s joystick when connected. Voice interaction is a proposed next step and is not represented as implemented.

What this project demonstrates

Thinking beyond screens: mapping physical inputs to digital actions, designing around context of use, and being explicit about the limits of an early prototype.

Before publishing, add real app screenshots, a short screen recording and a simple control-mapping diagram. The artwork above is an editorial placeholder, not a screenshot of the app.
